data.hypothesis: The selected row-parallel r-k-c parent is valid at 0.009476691 s. Earlier row-parallel variants with explicit SIMD and with k unrolling plus SIMD were also valid but slower (0.010415142 s and 0.009647238 s). This contrasting follow-up tiles each output row into 32 columns, accumulates each tile locally in ascending k order, then writes each output element once. It may reduce repeated C read-modify-write traffic, at the cost of accessing B in column chunks; the outcome is unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these results to motivate a distinct accumulator-blocking experiment, not to predict its performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid row-parallel r-k-c candidate measured 0.009476691 s, faster than the measured row-parallel SIMD variant at 0.010415142 s and unrolled SIMD variant at 0.009647238 s. The measurements establish those timings but not why the variants differed.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 32-column local-accumulator variant against the selected parent on all official sizes, including repeated native n=1024 timings.

data.notes: This candidate is based on selected parent 1db3e20bf05b4154 (base commit 8a35ddccb46a05fbabafb6a682854398f94e6acb). Each supported-size output element is initialized in a local zeroed accumulator and assigned once per call; the caller-provided thread budget remains capped by min(threads, N). The tail-width logic handles partial tiles. Unsupported sizes retain the prior zero-output behavior. No performance gain is claimed before controller measurement.
transformations: Retain static OpenMP parallelism over independent rows, capped by the caller-provided thread count.
Replace repeated output-element read-modify-write updates with a 32-column local accumulator tile; traverse k in ascending order and columns contiguously within each B chunk.
Assign every supported-size output element from a zero-initialized local accumulator; preserve zero-output behavior for unsupported sizes.
